question: Should this PR merge the per-reviewer-instance exact-input exec reviewer memo, with a 128-entry in-memory lifetime and command/session-sensitive key?
rationale: The code shape is narrow, but caching model-backed exec approval decisions changes when OpenClaw skips a fresh security review for a later request, so this needs explicit approval-boundary intent.

options.title: Approve scoped memo after proof
options.body: Keep the PR's per-instance exact-input memo, require redacted real-behavior proof, and treat adjacent Codex/plugin harness reuse as a separate follow-up if needed.

options.title: Narrow the cached outcomes
options.body: Ask the author to cache only selected conservative outcomes, such as low-risk allow-once, if maintainers do not want transient ask/error/timeout decisions reused.

options.title: Preserve fresh review semantics
options.body: Decline the cache and accept repeated reviewer completions until stronger security or billing evidence supports changing one-request-one-review behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped memo after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR's per-instance exact-input memo, require redacted real-behavior proof, and treat adjacent Codex/plugin harness reuse as a separate follow-up if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The current reviewer implementation and adjacent Codex exec-review trust work make this the strongest routing candidate for the cache-boundary decision.
